prompts.display_text: Pin the Hill Cumorah, where Joseph Smith received the gold plates in 1827.
prompts.text_original: Drop a pin on the Hill Cumorah near Palmyra, New York, where Joseph Smith received the gold plates from Moroni in 1827.
prompts.citation: Hill Cumorah page, ChurchofJesusChrist.org; Church History Topics, Angel Moroni, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: The Hill Cumorah is a drumlin in Manchester, New York, a few miles from the Smith family farm. Joseph Smith met the angel Moroni there each September from 1823 to 1827. On September 22, 1827, he received the gold plates from which he translated the Book of Mormon.

prompts.display_text: Pin a Latin American country with a dedicated temple named for a city other than its capital.
prompts.text_original: A Latin American country with a dedicated temple named for a city that is not its capital (as of November 2026).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronology and ChurchofJesusChrist.org temple list, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: Ten Latin American countries have dedicated temples in cities other than the capital. Brazil has eleven such temples and Mexico fourteen. Bolivia counts too, since Cochabamba is neither the constitutional capital Sucre nor the seat of government La Paz. Paraguay, Uruguay, Venezuela and the Central American one-temple countries do not qualify.

answers.name: Brazil
answers.fact: São Paulo, Recife, Porto Alegre and more (capital: Brasília).

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: Guadalajara, Monterrey, Tijuana and more (capital: Mexico City).

answers.name: Argentina
answers.fact: Córdoba, Salta, Mendoza and more (capital: Buenos Aires).

answers.name: Chile
answers.fact: Concepción, Antofagasta (capital: Santiago).

answers.name: Peru
answers.fact: Trujillo, Arequipa (capital: Lima).

answers.name: Colombia
answers.fact: Barranquilla (capital: Bogotá).

answers.name: Guatemala
answers.fact: Quetzaltenango, Cobán (capital: Guatemala City).

answers.name: Bolivia
answers.fact: Cochabamba (capital: Sucre (seat of government La Paz)).

answers.name: Ecuador
answers.fact: Guayaquil (capital: Quito).

answers.name: Honduras
answers.fact: San Pedro Sula (capital: Tegucigalpa).

prompts.display_text: Pin an African country an Apostle dedicated for the preaching of the gospel between 1983 and 1999.
prompts.text_original: An African country dedicated for the preaching of the gospel by an Apostle between 1983 and 1999 (other than Russell M. Nelson).
prompts.citation: Global Histories (churchofjesuschrist.org), country chronologies and overviews, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: After the 1978 revelation, Apostles crossed Africa dedicating nations: David B. Haight in Ghana (1983), Marvin J. Ashton in Zaire, Liberia and Cote d'Ivoire (1987) and Mauritius (1988), Richard G. Scott in Sierra Leone (1989), Republic of the Congo (1992) and Mozambique (1999), and James E. Faust in Kenya (1991).

answers.name: DR Congo
answers.fact: In August 1987 Elder Marvin J. Ashton dedicated Zaire for the preaching of the gospel.

answers.name: Ghana
answers.fact: In 1983 Elder David B. Haight, the first member of the Quorum of the Twelve to visit Ghana, dedicated the land for the preaching of the gospel.

answers.name: Cote d'Ivoire
answers.fact: In September 1987 Elder Marvin J. Ashton dedicated Cote d'Ivoire for the preaching of the gospel.

answers.name: Kenya
answers.fact: In 1991 Elder James E. Faust dedicated Kenya for the preaching of the gospel with more than 100 Church members present.

answers.name: Liberia
answers.fact: On September 2, 1987, Elder Marvin J. Ashton dedicated Liberia for the preaching of the gospel in Monrovia.

answers.name: Sierra Leone
answers.fact: In 1989 Elder Richard G. Scott, standing on Leicester Peak above Freetown, dedicated Sierra Leone for the preaching of the gospel.

answers.name: Republic of the Congo
answers.fact: In 1992 Elder Richard G. Scott, among the first Apostles to visit the country, dedicated the Republic of the Congo for the preaching of the gospel.

answers.name: Mozambique
answers.fact: In 1999 Elder Richard G. Scott of the Quorum of the Twelve dedicated Mozambique for the preaching of the gospel.

answers.name: Mauritius
answers.fact: In 1988 Elder Marvin J. Ashton of the Quorum of the Twelve dedicated Mauritius for the preaching of the gospel.

answers.name: Nigeria
answers.fact: In 1983 Elder David B. Haight rededicated Nigeria for missionary work; N. Eldon Tanner had first dedicated it in December 1962.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country outside the Americas where foreign missionaries were evacuated at the start of World War II, 1939 to 1941.
prompts.text_original: A country outside the Americas from which foreign missionaries were evacuated or called home at the start of World War II (1939-41), leaving local members to lead.
prompts.citation: Global Histories (churchofjesuschrist.org), country chronologies and overviews, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.note: Latin American withdrawals 1943-89 are a separate prompt; Brazil (1943) excluded here.
prompts.summary: As war spread in 1939 and 1940 the Church pulled North American missionaries out of Europe, the British Isles and the Pacific. Acting mission presidents and local members, such as Andre Anastasiou in Britain and Josef Roubicek in Czechoslovakia, carried the Church through the war years.

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: August 1939 to September 1940: as tensions escalated, missionaries throughout Europe were evacuated; Der Stern was discontinued by government policy in 1940.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: January 12, 1940: at the start of World War II missionaries from North America were evacuated and Andre K. Anastasiou was appointed acting British Mission president.

answers.name: Austria
answers.fact: 1939-45: American missionaries were evacuated and many Austrian Saints were drafted into the military.

answers.name: Denmark
answers.fact: December 2, 1939: American missionaries were withdrawn due to World War II and Orson Brinck West was appointed to lead.

answers.name: Australia
answers.fact: By January 1941 overseas missionaries had been evacuated; some branches continued under local leadership, many closed.

answers.name: Switzerland
answers.fact: 1939-46: American missionaries were evacuated from Europe and Swiss members filled leadership positions; Max Zimmer led.

answers.name: Czechia
answers.fact: August 24, 1939: missionaries were evacuated from Czechoslovakia prior to World War II; Josef Roubicek became acting mission president.

answers.name: Ireland
answers.fact: 1939-45: North American missionaries were evacuated from Ireland during World War II.

answers.name: New Zealand
answers.fact: October 15, 1940: with the onset of World War II, Church leaders instructed all missionaries in New Zealand to return home.

answers.name: Sweden
answers.fact: Foreign missionaries were evacuated from Sweden during the war; Fritz Johansson served as acting mission president.

answers.name: Slovakia
answers.fact: August 24, 1939: missionaries were evacuated from Czechoslovakia prior to World War II; Josef Roubicek became acting mission president.

answers.name: Tonga
answers.fact: 1940-46: World War II caused the evacuation of foreign missionaries; Emile C. Dunn remained as mission president over local member missionaries.

answers.name: Samoa
answers.fact: 1940-45: Samoan Saints assumed increased responsibility as missionaries were called home due to wartime conditions.
